newsitem.title: USA: Smell forces Delta landing at N.C. air force base.
newsitem.headline: Smell forces Delta landing at N.C. air force base.

text.p: A Delta Air Lines Inc passenger jet with 138 passengers on board made an unexpected landing at a North Carolina air force base on Friday when its pilot detected a strange odor, a company spokesman said.
"There was no emergency," said Todd Clay, a spokesman for the airline.

He said Delta Flight 1105, a McDonnell Douglas MD88 aircraft en route from Washington to Orlando, Florida, landed at Seymour Johnson Air Force Base near Goldsboro, North Carolina at about 4:25 p.m. EST (2125 GMT) after its pilot detected a strange smell.
He said the passengers left the plane using steps and there was no smoke and no fire.
"We are inspecting the aircraft now to see what caused the smell," Clay said.
He said the passengers remained at the base after the crash and that Delta was making arrangements for another aircraft to pick them up.
